name: volume_breakout_v178
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: This is an EVENT-driven strategy that fires rarely (1-3 times per day) but with high conviction. On NIFTY at 5-second resolution, a single bar with volume 5x its 60-bar average AND a simultaneous new session high or low represents an institutional order slamming into the book with extraordinary force — a single participant (or coordinated group) has committed capital so aggressively that they have consumed 5x normal liquidity AND pushed NIFTY to a level no one has reached all day. This dual requirement (extreme volume + new session extreme) is far more selective than either condition alone: volume spikes without new session extremes are common (block cross trades, index arbitrage rebalances) and carry limited directional information, while new session highs/lows on normal volume are gradual price discovery that often reverses. But when BOTH occur simultaneously on the same 5-second bar, it signals genuine directional conviction from a large participant who is willing to pay the market impact of crossing the entire available order book to establish a position. The continuation after such events is driven by two forces: (1) the large participant's order is likely not finished in a single 5-second bar and their remaining flow will push further, and (2) other algorithms detect the volume anomaly and session breakout and pile on. This strategy is fundamentally different from institutional flow momentum (which looks for single-bar volume spikes without requiring a new session extreme) — the session-extreme requirement is the critical filter that separates noise volume events from genuine directional conviction. We buy ATM CE when the event is a volume-climax new session high, and ATM PE for a volume-climax new session low.

indicators.name: volume_ratio_60
indicators.purpose: Ratio of the current bar's volume to the 60-bar (5-minute) average volume. The 60-bar lookback was chosen because on NIFTY at 5-second resolution, volume fluctuates significantly within each minute due to order batching and algo execution cycles. A 60-bar (5-minute) average smooths these micro-fluctuations and provides a stable baseline for what constitutes 'normal' volume in the current session phase. Shorter lookbacks (12-24 bars) are too noisy — a single large trade 30 seconds ago would inflate the average and make a genuinely extreme event look less extreme. We require > 5.0, meaning the bar has 5x the 5-minute average volume — an event that occurs only a handful of times per session.

indicators.name: session_high
indicators.purpose: The running session high. Used to detect when the current bar makes a NEW session high — meaning high > session_high[1] (the previous bar's session high). This is the price-extreme condition that, combined with volume_ratio_60 > 5, creates the full event signal. The session-level running maximum ensures we are comparing against the true day's high, not a rolling window high.

indicators.name: session_low
indicators.purpose: The running session low. Used to detect new session lows on the volume event bar. low < session_low[1] combined with the 5x volume condition creates the bearish event signal.

indicators.name: bar_close_position
indicators.purpose: Where the bar closed relative to its range — 1.0 means closed at the high, 0.0 means closed at the low. On the event bar, we require the close position to align with the breakout direction: > 0.6 for new session high events (the bar closed in its upper 40%, confirming the buyer held control through the full 5 seconds) and < 0.4 for new session low events. On NIFTY, volume-climax bars where the buyer pushes to a new high but then loses control within the same 5-second bar (close near the low) indicate the volume was absorption rather than initiation — the large order was met with equal counter-flow.

indicators.name: session_range_at_break
indicators.purpose: The session range at the moment of the volume-climax event. We require session_range > 20 spot points to ensure the session extreme being broken is a meaningful level. In the first 5-10 minutes of trading, the session 'high' and 'low' are trivially close together, and new session extremes are being set constantly with no significance. A 20-point minimum ensures enough price discovery has occurred for the extreme to represent genuine order accumulation.

indicators.name: minutes_since_open
indicators.purpose: Minutes elapsed since market open (09:15). Used to filter out the opening auction period (first 15 minutes = first 180 bars) where volume spikes are caused by the overnight order queue clearing, not by intraday institutional conviction. Also filters the last 30 minutes where volume spikes are closing-auction flows. The original strategy similarly excluded first 5 bars and last 10 bars on 1-minute data; on 5-second NIFTY data, the opening and closing distortion periods are longer in bars but similar in clock time.

conditions: volume_ratio_60 > 5.0 (current bar volume is 5x the 5-minute average — an extreme event on NIFTY that occurs only a few times per session)
high > session_high[1] (this bar makes a NEW session high — price has reached a level not seen all day)
bar_close_position > 0.6 (bar closed in its upper 40%, confirming the buyer maintained control through the full 5-second bar)
session_range_at_break > 20 (the session has established enough range that the session high is a meaningful level)
buy_ce.confirmation: The NEXT bar (confirmation bar) must also close above the previous session_high — meaning the new extreme holds for at least 10 seconds total (the event bar + confirmation bar). On NIFTY, volume-climax session-high events where the new high holds for 2+ bars continue upward ~60% of the time; those that reverse within the next bar are absorption events that revert ~65% of the time.

conditions: low < session_low[1] (this bar makes a NEW session low)
bar_close_position < 0.4 (bar closed in its lower 40%, confirming seller control)
buy_pe.confirmation: The next bar must also close below the previous session_low — new low holds for 2+ bars (10+ seconds).

exit.stop_rationale: A 5-option-point stop (roughly 10 spot points) is wider than most strategies because this is a HIGH-CONVICTION event signal — we want to give the trade room to absorb the post-event volatility without being stopped by noise. After a 5x volume bar at a new session extreme, the next 30 seconds on NIFTY are characteristically volatile as algorithms react to the event. A 10-spot-point adverse move through this noise is acceptable; a move beyond 10 points indicates the volume event was absorption (large participant selling INTO the new high), not initiation, and the trade thesis is wrong. On NIFTY, absorption events that look like breakouts typically reverse 12-20 spot points within 1-2 minutes.
exit.target_rationale: After a genuine volume-climax breakout to a new session extreme on NIFTY, the continuation wave typically carries 15-30 spot points (7-15 option points) over 1-3 minutes as the initiating participant's remaining order flow continues AND momentum algorithms activate. A 12-point target captures the core of this continuation (roughly 60-80% of the typical move) and provides a 2.4:1 reward-to-risk ratio. The larger target (vs 8-9 points for other strategies) is justified because the 5x volume condition selects for the most powerful institutional events where continuation is more pronounced. The original's 0.5% target on stocks would be ~110 spot points on NIFTY — far too ambitious for a 30-150 second hold.

filters.vix_filter: VIX between 11-30 — no strict lower bound needed because the 5x volume requirement self-selects for active markets. Above VIX 30, extreme volume bars become more frequent but less directionally informative (fear-driven liquidation creates volume spikes that reverse)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (first 15 minutes of opening auction distortion, and need 60 bars for volume_ratio_60 baseline) or after 14:30 — late-session volume spikes are often closing-auction mechanical flows with no directional intent
filters.volume_filter: The 5x volume ratio IS the core filter — by design, this is the most selective volume threshold of any strategy in the portfolio. It fires 1-3 times per day maximum on NIFTY
filters.trend_filter: Stronger edge when the volume-climax direction aligns with the day's VWAP trend: a 5x volume new session high when NIFTY is already above VWAP (bullish day) has ~65% continuation vs ~50% for a new high on a day trading below VWAP (counter-trend breakout)
filters.spread_filter: Skip if ATM option bid-ask > 3 points — at the moment of a volume climax, option market makers may briefly widen spreads, but given the higher target (12 points), a wider spread tolerance is acceptable

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — the 5x volume + session extreme dual requirement is extremely selective and difficult to front-run; the signal fires rarely enough that it does not attract systematic crowding

adaptation_notes: Four major changes from the original 1-minute stock-level volume breakout to 5-second NIFTY index options: (1) Volume baseline changed from SMA(volume, 20) on 1-minute bars (20-minute average) to SMA(volume, 60) on 5-second bars (5-minute average). This is NOT a blind 12x scaling: the 60-bar (5-minute) window was chosen because NIFTY's 5-second volume has significant micro-clustering where single seconds can have 3-5x the volume of neighboring seconds due to algo execution timing. A 5-minute baseline smooths these clusters to reveal genuinely extreme events. The 20-minute baseline from the original would over-smooth and make the 5x threshold too easy to trigger. (2) Added bar_close_position confirmation filter which the original included as part of entry conditions but we made more explicit. On 5-second bars, the close position within the bar is the key signal separating initiation (buyer holds control) from absorption (buyer is met with equal selling). This distinction is less critical on 1-minute bars where 60 seconds of price action is summarized, but on 5-second bars it is the primary quality filter. (3) Added 2-bar confirmation (event bar + next bar both above/below the old session extreme). The original required 'next bar also closes above previous session high' on 1-minute, which meant 1 minute of confirmation. On 5-second, we require 1 confirmation bar (5 additional seconds) — this is proportionally less time but sufficient because the 5x volume condition already provides much stronger conviction than the original's simple 'next bar' check. (4) Session range minimum (20 spot points) was added to filter the opening period. The original excluded first 5 bars on 1-minute (5 minutes) via a time filter; we use both a time filter AND a range minimum because on NIFTY at 5-second resolution, the session range can remain narrow even after 15 minutes on quiet days.
weaknesses: The 5x volume threshold means this strategy fires only 0-3 times per day on NIFTY, creating significant P&L concentration risk — a single loss erases multiple sessions of gains if position sizing is not disciplined

Some 5x volume events on NIFTY are caused by index arbitrage basket trades or ETF creation/redemption flows that hit the index at the session extreme by coincidence — these have no directional information and the close-position filter cannot fully distinguish them from genuine directional events

The 2-bar confirmation requirement means entering AFTER the 5x volume bar, by which time the option spread may have widened and the best entry price is gone — the institutional impact that created the event is already partially priced into ATM options within 5-10 seconds

On NIFTY weekly expiry days (Thursdays), delta hedging flows can create volume spikes at session extremes near popular strike prices that look identical to genuine institutional events but have no continuation — the volume is hedging, not directional positioning

In a crash or spike scenario (circuit breaker proximity), multiple 5x volume bars fire in sequence, each making new session extremes — the strategy may enter on the first and hit its stop as the market continues to move violently through the event, only to have subsequent signals work but capital is already committed
